newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE to strengthen Euromark futures ahead of EMU.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE to strengthen Euromark futures ahead of EMU.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Friday it will introduce two monthly expiries (serial futures) and four additional quarterly delivery months for the three-month Euromark interest rate futures contract on 13 January 1997.

LIFFE said in a statement that the three-month serial futures have the same contract specifications as the three-month Euromark. Four additional quarterly delivery months will be added to the three month Euromark contract, creating an additional fourth contract year.

"The introduction of further expiry months represents an additional initiative as part of LIFFE's strategy in preparation for Economic and Monetary Union," said Daniel Hodson, LIFFE's chief executive in a statement.
The move comes a month after LIFFE launched a one-month Euromark futures contract, aimed at supporting the London exchange's bid to become the centre for trading euro derivatives post-EMU.
LIFFE's German rival, Deutsche Terminboerse (DTB) launched its own one-month Euromark contract in November, and its new three-month Euromark future is due to start trading in January.
